title: AI changes *Nothing* — Dax Raad, OpenCode
talk_summary: Dax Raad argues that AI does not change the fundamentals of building a successful product: top-of-funnel marketing that earns attention, a single ruthless 'aha moment' with friction removed, and retention via composable primitives that serve both simple and advanced users. He explicitly says AI has not helped him with any of these, because they require creativity, clarity, and hard design thinking rather than generation.

takeaways.technique: Single 'aha moment' as the prioritization anchor
takeaways.what_they_do: Identify the one interaction that makes a user 'get' the product, then ruthlessly cut every step before it, deprioritizing all other features.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need to figure out what is the singular aha moment in your product and eliminate friction ruthlessly to get someone to that aha moment as fast as possible.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of building each feature directly, build wide, powerful primitive layers first, then assemble the simple 99% experience on top of them, exposing primitives directly to power users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of building the feature, you kind of have to build primitives that can be assembled into that feature.

takeaways.what_they_do: Be brutal about picking the one thing that matters and deprioritize everything else, rather than trying to surface all good features at once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You have to be brutal. You kind of have to like you know kill your children here.

takeaways.technique: Don't take shots with zero hit probability
takeaways.what_they_do: Only invest in efforts that could plausibly be a hit; skip the safe, obviously-mediocre moves entirely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't bother taking shots that never have a chance of being a hit, right? That's just a waste of time.

takeaways.technique: AI is weak at 'cool' — keep humans on positioning
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that AI brainstorming produces corny, unusable ideas for attention-grabbing marketing; creativity stays human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have not had a single good idea come out of AI.
